Reception New Starters 2026
Reception New Starters 2026
Welcome to Marsh Baldon CE Primary School
We are delighted to welcome our new families and children to join us in September 2026. We can’t wait to get to know you properly and integrate you into our school family. If you weren't able to secure a place, please put your name down on the waiting list with Oxfordshire County Council Admissions Team.
In the meantime, there is lots of information on the website under the Parents tab that you may find useful - School lunches; Uniform; After School Clubs and Breakfast Club; Wraparound Childcare. We have also added documents and guidance below that you may find useful, and please don't hesitate to contact us with anything that we can help with.
Carolyn Hanwell Lisa Scott-Russell
Headteacher Class Teacher
Being ready for school
School readiness may mean several things to different people. At Oxfordshire County Council we have adopted UNICEF’s description of the three elements of school readiness:
Children have the potential to become school ready when families, early years providers and schools work together to support the development of children’s confidence, resilience and curiosity.
A child who is ready for school will be:
Children’s readiness for school
Families and communities’ readiness for school
Settings’ and schools’ readiness for children.
Curious and confident about learning.
Resilient and ready to take part.
Confidently active and be healthy.
Independent with self-care skills.
Comfortable to make friends and take turns.
Cared for and feel safe and secure.
Able to vocalise choices.
Starting Reception

pageCache.pageTitle: Breakfast Club | Marsh Baldon Church of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
Breakfast Club
Funded Breakfast Club for ALL children, 8:10 - 8:40am
We are excited to be part of the government’s breakfast club early adopter scheme. (From summer term 2025, funded breakfast clubs are available in early adopter schools, as part of a test and learn phase, so that the government can plan for a full national roll-out of universal breakfast clubs in primary schools.)
As part of the offer, Marsh Baldon CE Primary School will offer 30 minutes of funded childcare alongside a free breakfast. The club is run by our Teaching Assistants, who take the children to their classrooms ready for morning registration.
Breakfast Club is open to all children from Reception to Year 6.
We ask that children attending this universal Breakfast Club arrive between 8:10 - 8:15am. This is when the gate is monitored, and allows enough time for food preparation and dining.
There is no need to pre-book these sessions - just turn up between 8:10 - 8:15am.
Early Birds Breakfast Club, from 7:30am arrival
Our 'Early Birds' Breakfast Club runs every day and is open to all year groups.
'Early Birds' is open from 7.30am each day. On arrival, please ring the bell at the entrance gate, and a member of staff will come and collect your child.
'Early Birds' sessions cost £3.40 and we ask that these sessions are booked in advance.
Regular weekly sessions can be paid for in advance either daily, weekly or termly. You can use Childcare vouchers to pay for these sessions.
The nutritional breakfast on offer may consist of: cereal; bagels, toast, yoghurts and fruit. All food offered is compliant with School Food Standards.
There will be a variety of indoor and outdoor activities on offer to engage the children, such as: board games, construction, drawing, reading, movement and calming activities (i.e. Cosmic Yoga, Danny Go!) and is a relaxed, social time to catch up with their friends before the start of the school day.

After School Childcare
Our wraparound childcare runs after school until 5.30pm Monday-Thursday, and until 4.15pm on a Friday. It runs every day the school is open.

About the School
'I came to give you life, life in all its fullness' John 10:10
Our Curriculum Design
Our Vision and Intent
We are passionate about nurturing our children to become compassionate, curious and knowledgeable global citizens in the 21st century. With this in mind, we have designed our curriculum with the golden thread of sustainability and environmental education woven throughout. Our aim is for children to engage deeply with the environment and understand that everyone can make a difference. We want our pupils to develop an understanding of environmental issues and challenges, while maintaining a sense of hope and connection with the natural world—both locally and globally.
